Median, Mean and Restricted Mean Survival of the Fitted Models

Source: R/survival_summary.R
survival_summary.Rd

Reports, for each fitted model and each arm it predicts, the median survival time, the mean survival time and, when time_horizon is given, the restricted mean survival time up to the time horizon, as computed by summary.flexsurvreg().

Usage

survival_summary(
  x,
  time_horizon = NULL,
  conf_int = FALSE,
  n_sim = 1000,
  seed = 1
)

Arguments

x

Object returned by fit_survival_models.

time_horizon

NULL (the default) or a single positive time horizon for the restricted mean, in the time unit of the data.

conf_int

Logical; TRUE to add simulated confidence limits. The default is FALSE.

n_sim

Number of simulated parameter vectors for the confidence limits. The default is 1000.

seed

Seed of the simulation, a single whole number. The default is 1.

Value

A data frame with the columns fit_type, arm (the arm predicted), model, median, median_lcl, median_ucl, mean, mean_lcl, mean_ucl, rmst, rmst_lcl and rmst_ucl (NA without time_horizon; the limits are NA without conf_int).

Details

The mean is the integral of the fitted survival function from 0 to infinity; it is infinite for heavy-tailed fits (for example a log-logistic shape of 1 or less) and for a Gompertz model with a negative shape, which leaves a proportion of patients who never have the event. Values that are not finite or cannot be computed are reported as NA. The confidence limits, when requested, are simulated as in predict_survival.

Examples

dat <- processing_dataset(
  system.file("extdata", "fit_example.csv", package = "SurvFitSummary"),
  column_arm = "TRT01P", column_survtime = "AVAL", column_cnsr = "CNSR",
  control_arm = "Control"
)
fits <- fit_survival_models(dat, distributions = c("exp", "weibull"),
                            spline_scales = NULL)
survival_summary(fits, time_horizon = 60)
